narration: We start with the captured data: K posed views of the scene, the RGB images I one through K, and alongside them the binary masks M one through K that mark the bear statue we want to remove.
Those views are fitted into a 3D Gaussian Splatting scene, G one through N. At this point the statue is still part of the reconstruction.
Rendering that scene from every camera gives the depth maps D one through K. This whole first stage is simply the Gaussians with the bear statue still in them.
The second stage works out where to inpaint. Take two of the views: the reference view, image I one with mask M one, and a neighbouring view, image I two with mask M two.
Applying each mask blacks the statue out of its own image, giving the background images I-B two and I-B one.
Using the depth map D two, the blacked-out region of view two is projected into view one and merged with it, producing I-B one-two.
What survives in both views is the region no camera can see behind the statue. Thresholding it yields M-prime one, the depth-guided inpainting mask.
That mask is carried into the third stage. A 2D inpainter fills it in, giving the inpainted reference image I-In one and its inpainted depth D-In one.
Depth-guided projection lifts those inpainted pixels back into 3D, producing the point cloud P one for the hole that the statue left behind.
Reprojecting that point cloud into the remaining cameras gives the projected views I-P two through K, pseudo-ground-truth for every other viewpoint.
The same point cloud also initializes new Gaussians, refining the scene into G-prime one through N-prime, now without the statue.
Rendering the refined scene from the reference camera gives I-prime one and D-prime one, which the render loss compares against the inpainted image and depth.
Rendering it from the other cameras gives I-prime two through K, which the cross loss compares against the projected views, keeping the fill consistent across viewpoints.
Together the three stages run end to end: reconstruct the scene with the statue, infer a depth-guided inpainting mask, then refine the Gaussians under inpainting guidance until the statue is gone.
